grh_2cf164dcc80890383416.title: Snow White
paragraphs: Snow White escapes the jealous queen and finds refuge with the seven dwarfs, but the queen disguises herself and tricks her into biting a poisoned apple. The dwarfs chase the witch through a storm until she falls from a cliff, yet they believe they are too late to save Snow White and place her in a glass-and-gold resting place. The prince who has searched for her arrives and wakes her with a kiss. Snow White says farewell to the dwarfs and rides with him toward his castle and the fairy-tale ending she had wished for.

Other credited names include Jerome Lawrence as radio adaptor, Robert E. Lee as radio adaptor, Gordon MacRae as host, and Marvin Miller as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 24 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.f7185f50dd01455d|Association of American Railroads]].
This version dramatizes [[work|work.rr.41727070400981d3|Snow White]]. Jerome Lawrence adapted it for radio and Robert E. Lee adapted it for radio.

grh_2c37ef4ee2e7a8c5399b.title: Borrowed Night
paragraphs: A dramatization of Oscar Ray's Borrowed Night follows an Alsatian forced into the German army who attempts to escape service by feigning traumatic neurosis. In a military hospital he watches German doctors expose other suspected malingerers and send them to execution, while his own deception becomes increasingly dangerous. After a fellow patient kills the doctor examining him, he escapes the hospital and crosses Germany, ending with his determination to regain his strength, join the French forces and return against the system he fled.

The cast includes Peter Capell, Guy Repp, Theo Goetz, William Malten, and Luis Van Rooten. Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director, Norman Winter as radio adaptor, and Jack Costello as host.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.75759ef2b267a8ba|Borrowed Night]]. Oscar Ray is credited as author and Norman Winter adapted it for radio.

grh_2cb0cd9dd53065990080.title: The Trouble with Women
paragraphs: Reporter Kate Farrell writes a sensational article about psychology professor Gilbert Sedley that leaves her newspaper facing a major libel suit, including the claim that he believes in hitting women. To manufacture proof, Kate enrolls in Sedley's class under cover and repeatedly tries to provoke him into striking her. Instead the combative experiment turns into romance, and the escalating deception finally spills into court, where psychology, hypnosis and Kate's real feelings undo the scandal she set out to create.

grh_2c6ce39023edb14e2ad3.title: Hold Back the Dawn
